newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba allots 74.7 bln marks in repo, adds funds.
newsitem.headline: Buba allots 74.7 bln marks in repo, adds funds.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Wednesday that it allocated 74.7 billion marks in securities repurchase funds at a three percent fixed rate.
The central bank said it accepted 27.0 percent of the bids.
A repo pact for 72.1 billion marks, also set at a fixed three percent rate, expires Wednesday, so a net 2.6 billion marks is flowing into the market.
The Bundesbank said banks bid for 276.7 billion marks of the repurchase funds this week. The Bundesbank has kept its main money market rate, the repo, fixed at three percent since August 1996.
Money market traders had been predicting an addition of about one billion marks of funds in this week's tender.

If the central bank had sharply cut back on the amount of liquidity available to the market the allocation could have been seen as reinforcing speculation that the central bank was on the point of raising its securities repurchase rate.

In a break with the tradition established over the last year, the central bank has not yet announced the conditions at which it will offer repo funds next week, leading to talk it could be about to raise the rate to support a weak mark.
